name: Engineering Deck
narrativeOnEnter: Cramped and hot. Conduit panels cover every wall. The main junction box hangs open — someone started the reroute and stopped. A wiring schematic is taped inside the panel cover. Below, an access tunnel leads to the cargo bay and reactor.

action.text:
LIFE SUPPORT POWER REROUTE — ENGINEERING MANUAL
Taped inside panel cover — DO NOT REMOVE

Emergency connection order:
  Red   → Junction A  (High voltage — connect first)
  Blue  → Junction D
  Green → Junction B
  Yellow→ Junction C  (Low voltage — connect last)

Incorrect wiring will trip the breaker and count as a system fault.
Complete sequence restores life support and unseals command blast doors.

ENGINEERING LOG — KOVALEV, D.

Entry 110 (3 days ago):
'Found an anomalous network node mounted inside the reactor housing superstructure.
Not in the original build spec. Signal traces back to the main bus buffer.
I pulled the log. The node has been transmitting telemetry for 63 days — since launch.
The telemetry isn't reactor data. It's biometric. Neural pattern waveforms.
I know what this is. I worked adjacent to this kind of research before joining the crew.
They're called Synaptic Response Recorders.
Someone put six of them on this station. One per crew member.
We've been mapped. All of us. For 63 days.
The buffer is full. That's what MERIDIAN-3 is waiting for — a clean extraction.'

Entry 111 (yesterday):
'I found the Cargo Bay container with the other units. Original shipping: Δ Medical Dynamics.
Parent company: AXIOM Group. Charter for this station: HELIOS GROUP — also AXIOM.
This was never a science posting. We were the science.
Chen knows. Diaz and the others evacuated — I don't know what they were told.
I've identified two options: delete the buffer (requires physical access to the node),
or trigger a controlled thermal event that wipes it as a side effect.
The thermal event is survivable. Probably.'

Entry 112 (today):
'Reactor temperature is off by 40%. I caused that — started the thermal sequence.
Had to abort mid-way when the alarm triggered. Need to complete the reroute first.
Gone to Reactor Deck to manually stabilise and finish it.

If anyone finds this:
— Finish the wiring first (schematic is on the panel)
— Cargo Bay lock sequence is on the freight manifest
— Reactor stabilisation sequence is in the safety manual on Reactor Deck
If I don't make it back, pod bay code is on Chen's ID.

If the buffer burns: we're just six crew members again. Not cargo.
Not data.
Not PROMETHEUS.
— D. Kovalev'
